B00064NW28.retailer_description: The Fava Bean (Vica faba) is a flat, oval bean, 3/4 to 1 inch long, that grows in an inedible large pod. Penne Rigate are part of the short, diagonal cut, ridged pasta family and are one of the most well-known type of pasta, as well as being the most versatile in the kitchen. In Italian, the term "Penne" refers to the goose feather which was used historically to write with and was cut on a diagonal to achieve a really thin tip. The shape, obtained from a pasta tube, can be smooth or ridged, of varying length and has the typical diagonal cut of a quill. Penne are one of the few types of pasta for which there is an exact date when it was created. Indeed, in 1865, a pasta-maker from San Martino d'Albaro (Genoa), Giovanni Battista Capurro, requested and obtained a patent for a diagonal cutting machine. The patent was important because it meant the fresh pasta could be cut like a quill without crushing it and in different lengths from 3 to 5 centimetres (mezze "half" penne or penne). The document preserved in the Central Archive of the State of Rome reads: "Up until now, a diagonal cut could only be made by hand with a pair of scissors which, in addition to being slow and time-consuming, also resulted in an irregular cut which flattened the pasta". Penne Rigate are perfect for preparing oven-baked pasta or pasta dishes served with meat sauces made from pork or beef. This pasta is equally as good with vegetable based sauces and more in general, due to its versatility, for any recipe from the Mediterranean tradition, such as the classic condiment with tomato, basil, extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkling of parmesan. A classic combination is with Arrabbiata sauce. Available in 16.0 oz and 5 lb.

Historically, official mention of the term "spaghetto" can be traced back to the first dictionary of the Italian language by Nicolò Tommaseo and Bernardo Bellini (1819). The word "spaghetto" was included as the "masculine singular diminutive of spago (thread)" and mention is made of "Minestra di Spaghetti" (spaghetti soup) which is pasta the size of a long, thin thread such as sopracapellini". An interesting fact: in 1957, the BBC aired the first documentary on the production of spaghetti and the day after, the television studios were inundated by phone calls from viewers asking for the name of the producers and distributors of spaghetti so they could buy some. B0016H989U.retailer_description: Our original name, La Crema Viñera, means “best of the vine,” setting the standard for all we do since 1979. For more than 40 years, our family-owned and operated winery has focused exclusively on cool-climate appellations, from our original home in the Russian River Valley, to Monterey and now the Willamette Valley. We’re continually exploring these very special regions—passionate in our belief that they make uniquely expressive and elegant wines. We select vineyards that fall within cool mesoclimates and possess well-drained soils, which naturally restricts yields and produces distinctive, balanced wines. Our grapes ripen slowly and see long hang time, allowing complex flavors and aromas and firm acid structure to develop. Our vineyard site selection and boutique winemaking techniques ensure the consistently distinct, naturally balance wines we are committed to producing. In the summer of 2016, La Crema settled into a new home, nestled within the storied Saralee’s Vineyard in the heart of the Russian River Valley. Here, we’ve created a premier destination for unparalleled wine education and culinary explorations. Planted in 1988 by Saralee Kunde and her husband Richard, Saralee’s Vineyard was carefully tended by the couple and has a reputation for producing some of the finest grapes in California. The cool climate, varied terrain and diverse soils provide an ideal environment for a wide range of varietals, particularly Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Built in the late 1800s, an historic building sits atop a knoll on the sprawling property, overlooking rolling vineyards. Originally a barn, the Kunde’s transformed the building into their family home, and now the story continues as the striking structure begins its third phase as a tasting room and winery destination for La Crema. Revered by the community for her agricultural advocacy and contributions to local organizations, including strong support of Sonoma’s 4-H Center and Future Farmers of America, Saralee Kunde built a legacy that we are honored to carry on.

B0016H9912.retailer_description: Characterized by the winemaking process that focuses on pure fruit expression, Whole Cluster refers to making wine with entire bunches of grapes including the stems, a style that was common until the invention of destemming machines. What happened next was magical − the berries started to swell and turn pink. When they burst, they released the most aromatic, fermenting Pinot Noir. Willamette Valley Vineyards Whole Cluster Pinot Noir is balanced, refreshing and versatile for countless food pairings.

B003CJ8WHY.retailer_description: Experience the gentle revolution in hair color with Naturcolor’s innovative botanical-based formula. Unlike conventional dyes that strip hair with harsh chemicals and deposit monotone dye, our unique approach uses just enough chemistry to enable Naturcolor’s fine Italian pigments to adhere to each strand, preserving hair's natural variation while effectively covering gray. The result? Rich, multi-dimensional color that looks authentically yours with significantly less risk of irritation or damage. Our nourishing botanical blend actually improves shine, strength, and overall health with every application. Naturcolor fits easily into your life with a refreshingly pleasant experience that minimizes harsh odors and mess. What was once a necessary chore becomes a moment of intentional self-care, leaving you with healthy, vibrant hair that helps you feel ready for whatever comes your way. With Naturcolor, you never need to choose between beautiful, lustrous locks and your personal well-being. Crafted in small batches in California since 1992, Naturcolor is not just for women. Thousands of men have discreetly colored their hair with it at home. And the gentler formula is great for coloring facial hair without irritation or staining. Naturcolor comes in 31 colors that can be blended to create your own unique shade. A complete application takes less than an hour and one box can be used for multiple root touch-ups. Note: Final results will vary based on original hair color. Hair that is much lighter than your selected Naturcolor shade will appear lighter after coloring, while hair closer to the Naturcolor shade will take on a deeper, more intense color. This variability also applies to gray hair, which will take color differently than darker strands, contributing to the dimensional results that make Naturcolor look natural and never “dyed”.

B006KC7KF0.retailer_description: Our Lavender Facial Tonic Hydrosol is sourced from a few small, organic farms. It is distilled solely for its hydrophilic (water-loving) components, not the essential oil. Distillers of essential oils usually use plant material that has been dried over several days, resulting in a loss of approximately 70% of water volume. We choose to distill for the hydrosol alone and use only fresh plant material. In this way the resulting hydrosol is much richer in the valuable, water-soluble aromatic molecules. Furthermore, these hydrosols are artisan-distilled at low temperatures for over two to three hours. Conventional distillation utilizes high temperatures, and the process lasts for only thirty to forty-five minutes. The more labor-intensive artisan process that we choose to use creates a hydrosol that is vitalizing and healing for all skin conditions. Pure plant hydrosols are some of nature's best antioxidants. They play an important role in protecting the skin from free radicals and pollution. Saturating the skin daily with these precious waters restores pH balance, refreshes and tones skin tissue, maintaining soft and smooth skin while significantly increasing vitality and hydration to all skin conditions. B007QY6YXU.retailer_description: Our original name, La Crema Viñera, means “best of the vine,” setting the standard for all we do since 1979. For more than 40 years, our family-owned and operated winery has focused exclusively on cool-climate appellations, from our original home in the Russian River Valley, to Monterey and now the Willamette Valley. We’re continually exploring these very special regions—passionate in our belief that they make uniquely expressive and elegant wines. We select vineyards that fall within cool mesoclimates and possess well-drained soils, which naturally restricts yields and produces distinctive, balanced wines. Our grapes ripen slowly and see long hang time, allowing complex flavors and aromas and firm acid structure to develop. Our vineyard site selection and boutique winemaking techniques ensure the consistently distinct, naturally balance wines we are committed to producing. In the summer of 2016, La Crema settled into a new home, nestled within the storied Saralee’s Vineyard in the heart of the Russian River Valley. Here, we’ve created a premier destination for unparalleled wine education and culinary explorations. Planted in 1988 by Saralee Kunde and her husband Richard, Saralee’s Vineyard was carefully tended by the couple and has a reputation for producing some of the finest grapes in California. The cool climate, varied terrain and diverse soils provide an ideal environment for a wide range of varietals, particularly Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Built in the late 1800s, an historic building sits atop a knoll on the sprawling property, overlooking rolling vineyards. Originally a barn, the Kunde’s transformed the building into their family home, and now the story continues as the striking structure begins its third phase as a tasting room and winery destination for La Crema. Revered by the community for her agricultural advocacy and contributions to local organizations, including strong support of Sonoma’s 4-H Center and Future Farmers of America, Saralee Kunde built a legacy that we are honored to carry on.

B007SDV71I.retailer_description: Tommasi has always been a standard bearer of the Amarone appellation, and one of the most important quality producers in the Veneto. Established in 1902 around the family home in Pedemonte in Valpolicella, the winery has grown and expanded into the choicest areas of the region under the guidance of the many generations of the Tommasi family. The winery is known above all for its classic approach to winemaking in Valpolicella, favoring elegance and balance, and paying homage to the winemaking tradition of their home region. The family owns 284 acres in Valpolicella Classico, making them the single largest land owners in the area. Over the years they have steadily expanded their holdings in other areas of the Veneto and other regions, and now own a total of 1,400 acres under vine between the Veneto, Tuscany, Puglia, Basilicata and Oltrepo Pavese. As has been the case since the winery’s establishment, the family works only with grapes they grow, an important quality decision and reflection of their deep connection to the Valpolicella soil. Tommasi is now run by the fourth generation of the family, six siblings and cousins who share different responsibilities at the winery. Giancarlo Tommasi is the principal winemaker, and studied winemaking the University of Udine in Friuli. Strict in his philosophy to respect the integrity of the terroir and the traditional ways of winemaking in Valpolicella, he dries all grapes for his Amarone in the traditional fruttaio room for at least three months, and prefers to age his wines in large oak casks over small barriques. Tommasi is known for this classic approach that favors elegance and balance, with deep fruit complimented by spicy, earthy flavors. Giancarlo’s uncle, Sergio Tommasi, manages the viticulture at the estate. The five valleys of San Ambrogio, San Pietro in Cariano, Fumane, Marano and Negrar dominate the western, best and Classico-designated part of the region, and are often said to resemble the fingers of a hand. Tommasi’s vineyards are located in two of these valleys: Sant’ Ambrogio and San Pietro in Cariano. While they have a very traditional approach in the cellar, Tommasi is considered an innovator in the way they manage their vineyards. Tommasi was one of the first wineries to introduce the guyot method over the more traditional pergola system of vine-training, and their vineyards are planted at very high density, with resulting lower yields and fruit of increased complexity and concentration.

B00BX9NYX2.retailer_description: Bright, balanced, and unmistakably real. Numi's Aged Earl Grey opens with a robust black tea base and finishes with a bright, citrusy lift from real bergamot — no artificial flavoring, no perfume-like aftertaste. It's smooth enough to sip plain, bold enough to take milk, and holds its flavor beautifully over ice. That balance comes from time. We age organic Assam black tea with true bergamot oil for several weeks, allowing the citrus to fully infuse into the leaf rather than simply coating it. The result is a rounder, more integrated cup than teas flavored with bergamot essence alone. We start with fuller leaf, hand-plucked Assam from Tonganagaon, the largest organic Fair Trade tea estate in India. Larger leaves have more surface area to unfurl and steep evenly, releasing flavor gradually instead of the fast, tannic bitterness typical of machine-picked fannings and dust used in many tea bags. Sourcing from Tonganagaon also means your tea purchase supports Numi's Together for H2OPE project, which has brought clean water and sanitation to more than 6,500 farming families at the estate. Every tea bag is made from manila hemp (Abacá) fiber, sealed with a crimp-and-knot process instead of the plastic heat-seals used in most tea bags, so no polypropylene ever touches your cup. The bags are BPI Certified Biodegradable and supplier-verified free of added plastics or microplastics — not just labeled that way. The outer wrapper is plant-based and commercially compostable, made from FSC-certified paper and non-GMO sugarcane. Each bag is USDA Certified Organic and Fair Trade Certified. Steep 3–5 minutes in fresh, boiling water for a classic cup, hot or iced.

B00MN6GJGI.retailer_description: From vineyard to bottling, Special Cuvée sees such an extraordinary level of care and attention, it is difficult to place within the non-vintage or, really, any Champagne category. It is a Champagne that stands apart.  Within one bottle, all the complexity of flavor, texture and pleasure that Champagne can offer.  Special Cuvée is truly a journey of devotion from Bollinger.  Bollinger is the producer most associated with a single grape variety in Champagne, namely Pinot Noir. This more difficult grape to grow makes up a minimum of 60% of all of Bollinger’s Champagne. The harmony of Pinot Noir’s richness and elegance plays a large part in Special Cuvée’s distinct profile, the ripe red berries and powerful impact a clear signature. Then there is the other association that Bollinger is so well known for: winemaking in barrel. As virtually every Champagne producer in the latter half of the 20th century moved to fermenting in large lots in stainless steel tanks, Bollinger persisted to oversee fermentation barrel by barrel for all vintage Champagnes and a remarkable 30% of Special Cuvée. Why? Because the development of flavors becomes so much more complex, and the texture rounder and silkier. A third Bollinger specialty is the aging of Champagnes. Most Champagnes on the market are primarily made up of the most recently harvested vintage before requirements to age in bottle. Bollinger is primarily made up of Champagnes that are not from the most recent vintage, and in the end a newly released bottle of Bollinger is around 7-8 years old. A fourth – and utterly distinct – practice at Bollinger is the use of Reserve Magnums. The best vineyards will be aged under cork in magnum for up to 15 years, and hand disgorged into the final blend to bring the aromas and flavors only a great aged Champagne can display, notes such as truffles, ginger and walnut. So you have it all: the freshness that Champagne brings naturally, the secondary notes as the fruit character becomes riper and savory and spicy notes enter, and the third level, when fruit becomes almost crystallized, texture becomes like velvet, and the glass in front of you brings meaning to you and with those you have chosen to share. Special Cuvée does all of this for you.

B07285NWFT.retailer_description: Pure Tupelo honey is one of the most celebrated raw honey varieties in the world, and for good reason. This raw Tupelo Honey captures the brief White Tupelo bloom from southern river basins. Beekeepers wait all year for a narrow window to collect nectar with an unmistakable flavor. The result is a smooth, clear sweetness with a clean finish that feels elegant on the palate. It is pourable, spoonable, and enjoyable for anyone who loves real honey. What sets Tupelo honey apart is its naturally slow crystallization and silky texture. While ordinary honey can turn gritty or cloudy, Tupelo often stays fluid longer, which means easier drizzles over warm biscuits, yogurt, pancakes, and ice cream. Tea and coffee lovers appreciate how quickly it dissolves without overpowering aromas. Home cooks use it to add depth to marinades salad dressings glazes, and baked goods because it brings sweetness without heaviness. Our Tupelo honey pays homage to the region's heritage. For generations, beekeepers have worked near the blooming Tupelo trees along the Georgia and Florida rivers, waiting for a few weeks each spring. When the blossoms open, the bees get to work. When the blossoms fall, the season ends until the next year. This rhythm makes each jar feel special and adds a sense of rarity. Choosing this honey means choosing flavor first. The taste is buttery and floral with a light body that finishes clean. It does not cling to the tongue, and it does not leave a heavy, syrupy aftertaste. Chefs, food enthusiasts, and tea drinkers reach for Tupelo when they want ingredients to shine because it delivers sweetness that supports rather than dominates. So, how do you use it? Stir a spoon into hot tea or drizzle over toast. Try a ribbon over goat cheese or Greek yogurt. Add it to oat bowls, smoothies, fruit salad,s and roasted vegetables. Brush it on grilled salmon or chicken for a glossy finish. Or go simple and eat it straight off the spoon.

B076TMF3J7.retailer_description: Raeburn is an Olde English term which means "the river where one goes to drink." Chardonnay and Pinot Noir grapes benefit greatly from this maritime influence which fosters a longer more temperate growing season and yields fill flavored, complex wines with well-balanced acidity. B086ZFM5D2.retailer_description: Peet's Big Bang Medium Roast Coffee is our signature medium roast created to celebrate Alfred Peet and our 50th anniversary. Some have described Alfred Peet as the "big bang" of craft coffee, the one who started it all. When he set up shop in Berkeley back in 1966, he transformed America's expectations of the depth, body, and flavor in our cups. And that pursuit of greatness has never stopped. In 2016, we honored his legacy by taking a bold step ahead. Like Mr. Peet's pioneering dark roasts, this blend expands the horizon of what coffee can be: vibrant, full-flavored, boldly original, and roasted to medium-bodied perfection. If you love Major Dickason's one-of-a-kind taste, you'll find a kindred spirit in Big Bang. This blend is crafted from some of the same premium coffees as Major Dickason's but with a twist, thanks to the heavenly, aromatic citrus of Ethiopian Super Natural. It's the perfect coffee to honor the man who still inspires us every day.

B086ZFM5D9.retailer_description: Peet's Major Dickason's Blend Dark Roast Coffee is the roast that put Peet's Coffee on the map. A loyal customer of our original Berkeley store, retired army sergeant Key Dickason, brought the idea for our most beloved blend to Mr. Peet in 1969. Intrigued, our founder worked with the local gourmand and coffee aficionado to refine it. They sampled countless combinations before arriving at what is now our all-time bestseller. The result was so good, Alfred Peet decided naming it after his friend wasn't enough. Dickason's rich, complex blend also deserved a promotion from sergeant to major. Major Dickason's combines the best origin coffees from the world's premier growing regions, each imparting its distinctive regional characteristics while still effortlessly rounding into a smooth, balanced cup. Over the years, it has become the coffee that epitomizes Peet's: flavorful, deeply roasted, and unsurpassingly satisfying. But for us, "Major D" is just like a relationship with an old friend. We'll always remember it as the story of a customer's passion, an expert's palate, and a shared love of coffee.

B08N15B3NZ.retailer_description: Our story began in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, in 2012 with two childhood friends who wanted to create a place to celebrate coffee. At the core, we started with a commitment to source coffee through lasting relationships and roast quality coffee that highlights those as they should be. We opened our flagship roastery, education lab, and cafe on North 6th Street to create a space for coffee that is fun, approachable, and social. As our community grew, we did too: new spaces, new partners, new food, new relationships at origin, and of course, new coffee. Since then, our partnerships with farmers, producers, baristas, roasters, businesses, and customers have helped us to grow and nurture a shared coffee culture and experience in the city and beyond. We believe that we’re only as great as the sum of our partners. As partners in coffee, we thank you for being part of our journey, shaping our community, and helping us become who we are today. Partners Coffee is built on the strength of our lasting relationships at origin. We source coffee from around the world from people we know and trust—to produce beautiful coffee, and be the greatest stewards of the land they grow upon. We focus on relationships. We aspire to purchase from the same producers and communities year after year and to work directly with producers when possible. Our goal is to promote mutual, long-term success through communication and shared growth. Maintaining strong relationships at origin allows Partners to offer blends with a consistent flavor profile while celebrating talented producers through their seasonally rotating single origin menu. We believe in comprehensive purchasing. Even the best coffee farms produce a spectrum of quality. We consider this and strategize large, meaningful purchases—where we buy microlots and seek dependable volume coffees. Through the careful purchasing of non-commodity priced coffee, Partners builds secure supply chains that enable farmers to invest in local communities.

Susan & Tara met on their first day of their master's program at LSE and fell into an instant best friendship. The idea for the business started on a classic BFF bathroom trip between lectures. Susan wanted to start a Fempire, while Tara couldn't find organic tampons anywhere in the UK. Susan was like, 'Organic tampons? Why do you even need those? A long chat about the impact of irritating chemicals, many late nights, and a master's dissertation later, and Here We Flo was born. We are a proudly women-owned and led, B-CORP business on a mission to empower people with periods to feel crazy confident even when it’s messy. At Here We Flo, we treat period care as personal care, not sanitary hygiene. Because your vagina deserves better. We create “better for you” accessible upgrades for period, pee, and pleasure that are better for vaginas + vulvas. Using materials that you can trust to work. No drama. No bad vibes. Just premium vulva experiences. Crazy confidence is all about how you feel inside. So we fight shame and stigma around periods, pee, and pleasure with a funny, feminist, + fierce personality and empower our community with actually useful information. We’re also committed to giving 5% of profits back to people + planet. Welcome to the Fempire, bestie.

B0DW1NFQSK.retailer_description: At La Tourangelle, we are passionate about creating high-quality ingredients that are good for the table, the community, and the planet. Our California Extra Virgin Olive Oil is sourced from a family-owned and operated ranch located in the rolling hills of the Capay Valley between Napa & Sacramento - just twenty minutes away from the La Tourangelle artisan oil mill in Woodland, CA. The olives are cold-pressed within hours of harvest to maximize oil quality and ensure freshness. La Tourangelle is one of the few remaining oil mills keeping a time-honored French heritage of roasting and pressing nut kernels into delicious oils. We are a family-owned company whose mastery of oil production is the fruit of passion, integrity, and pride. We strive to be the best artisanal oil producer, dedicated to crafting carefully selected, sustainable products. With artisanal care, we extract the essence and hidden natural treasures to create amazing products that bring delight to the kitchen and well-being to the body.

B0DWC2N1RR.retailer_description: Our Beginnings. When our founder, Steven, and his wife, Sara Jade, became parents, they placed a newfound value on living a more natural, sustainable lifestyle. In Sara Jade’s search for clean personal care products, she became frustrated by confusing natural claims and long, complicated ingredient lists, and learned that only products with an organic certification can be trusted to be pure, less processed, and more effective than commonly available alternatives. This inspired them to create their own products, and Sky Organics was born. Simple, Botanically-Based Solutions. Our products are thoughtfully curated to complement and enhance your clean beauty routine, and are formulated with as few ingredients as possible. We only include ingredients that we know will effectively deliver desired benefits, and we offer many single-ingredient products because that is often all that is truly needed to effectively care for skin, hair, lashes, or eyebrows. Integrity and Transparency. Because organic is known to be the cleanest form of natural and is clearly defined and certified, we seek out organic ingredients whenever available. We know for certain that our ingredients are sustainably grown, harvested without chemicals or synthetic fillers, and maintain their natural integrity and potency. When we do occasionally use a non-organic ingredient, it’s always a thoughtful choice that weighs the ingredient’s beauty benefit versus its organic availability, and we clearly communicate this on our product labels. Created for All. It's important to us that clean, natural, organic solutions are available to and affordable for as many people as possible, regardless of who they are, what they look like, or where they live. With this in mind, we offer self care essentials for every skin type and hair type, with a wide variety of beauty benefits and uses. Join Our Journey. We invite you to redefine your everyday approach to beauty and embrace a more hopeful world with Sky Organics.

BT00KQAOJW.retailer_description: Clean,vibrant palate. Refreshing throughout. Notes of apricot and Kaffir lime leaf on the nose and juicy tangerine flavors, with a long, mineral-driven finish. A magically flexible wine with food, the Adelsheim Chardonnay will pair with fresh seafood, roasted vegetables, poultry, or easy foods like chips & salsa. David Adelsheim's visit to Burgundy in the 1970s played a pivotal role in bringing "Dijon clones" of Chardonnay to America. This wine is made entirely from those clones and it represents the signature style of the Willamette Valley - intense aromatics and fruit character, fresh acidity, rich texture, and minimal oak influence.
